title: This One or That One?
description: Compare and choose between nearby and more distant items.
objectives: Compare and choose between nearby and more distant items.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to compare and choose between nearby and more distant items. The central language is this/that and one as a substitute noun. It belongs to the practical context of shopping & everyday english. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: this/that and one as a substitute noun

blocks.english: Do you prefer this one or that one?
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the this one or that one? exchange.
This this one or that one? model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the this one or that one? exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “Do you prefer this one or that one?” and “I like the red one.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: this/that and one as a substitute noun.
